name: Two-system reconciliation
problem: The same business object lives in two or more systems, each edited by different people on different rhythms. The copies drift, nobody notices until a total fails to tie out at close, and then someone spends days playing detective across exports.
signals: A recurring 'true-up' spreadsheet exists, and one person knows how to produce it.
Two departments quote different numbers for the same thing, and both are right in their own system.
Someone maintains a mental list of records that are 'known to be off'.
not_for: One of the systems can simply be retired. Reconciliation is life support for a migration that should just happen — price the migration before building the machine that papers over its absence.
A vendor-supported real-time sync exists and fits. Buy it, and spend the engagement on something the market has not solved.

The systems disagree on meaning, not values. If two departments define the object differently, that is the glossary's problem first — reconciliation code will faithfully propagate the confusion at machine speed.

steps: Enumerate records from the source of truth over the reconciliation window.
Fetch counterparts from each copy by the join key, applying the entity's identifier caveats.
Compare field-by-field over the compared set — an explicit list of fields, never 'everything'.
Classify each difference: missing-copy, stale-copy, conflicting-edit, or orphan.
Auto-apply only the classes declared safe, always in the direction of authority.
Queue conflicting-edits and orphans for the human adjudicator with both versions side by side.
Publish a drift report with the trend, not just the count.
base_shape.state: The last window reconciled, per-record fingerprints for cheap diffing, and the adjudication queue. Fingerprints let incremental runs skip the unchanged majority.
commitments: Authority has a direction, declared per entity in the manifest (source_of_truth) — never inferred at runtime, never bidirectional.
Conflicting human edits are never auto-resolved. The machine detects; a person adjudicates; the pattern of adjudications teaches the process.
The drift rate is the product. Rising drift means an upstream process changed — the report is an early-warning instrument, not a cleanup log.

variation_points.question: Full sweep every run, or incremental with fingerprints?

options.when: Volume makes full sweeps slow or expensive against rate limits.
options.consequence: Fast and cheap; fingerprint drift and deleted records can hide until a full pass.

options.when: Volume is small enough to compare everything every time.
options.consequence: Nothing hides; runtime and API cost grow linearly with the dataset forever.

variation_points.default_because: Incremental with a periodic full sweep — weekly or monthly — gets both properties: cheap routine runs, and a bounded window in which deletions and fingerprint drift can hide.

variation_points.question: Fix safe drift classes automatically, or report everything first?

options.when: Always, for the first weeks of a new instantiation.
options.consequence: No risk; humans still do the fixing while the report earns trust and reveals which classes are actually safe.

options.when: The report has run long enough to show which classes are mechanical and which hide judgment.
options.consequence: The toil disappears; a misclassified class now propagates errors in the direction of authority, so the classification itself needs a decision entry.

variation_points.default_because: You do not yet know which drift classes are safe — the report is how you learn. Graduating a class to auto-fix should be a recorded decision with the evidence attached.

variation_points.question: Where does the conflict queue live?

options.when: The client already has a worked review queue from another flow.
options.consequence: One queue, one habit, one staffing problem instead of two.

options.when: The adjudicator is a different person with different authority than existing queue operators.
options.consequence: Clean separation; a second queue that can be forgotten — instantiate human-review-queue properly, alarms included.

variation_points.default_because: Every additional queue is an additional staffing dependency with its own bus factor. Consolidate until authority boundaries force separation.

glue_checklist.question: How reliable is the join key, really?
glue_checklist.why_it_matters: The entity's identifier caveats decide feasibility. A reused or scoped identifier makes naive reconciliation actively destructive — it will 'fix' records into the wrong counterparts.

glue_checklist.question: Which fields actually need to agree?
glue_checklist.why_it_matters: Reconciling fields nobody reads is pure alarm noise, and noise is how drift reports get ignored. The compared set should be the fields a discrepancy in which costs money or trust.
glue_checklist.recorded_in: decisions[] (the compared-set decision, with what was deliberately excluded)

glue_checklist.question: What do void, cancelled, and deleted mean in each system?
glue_checklist.why_it_matters: Soft-deleted records that still appear in queries are the classic double-count — the reference manifest's VOID-loads quirk is the canonical example. A tombstone in one system and a live record in the other is drift only if you have defined which one is right.

glue_checklist.question: Who adjudicates conflicts, and with what authority?
glue_checklist.why_it_matters: Conflicting-edit resolution is a business decision wearing a technical costume. The adjudicator needs the standing to overrule whichever department made the losing edit.

human_roles.does: Decides conflicting edits and orphans. Their pattern of decisions IS the missing business rule — mine it, then propose automating the stable part.
human_roles.cadence: After each run; volume should trend toward zero as upstream causes get fixed.
transition_walkthrough_must_cover: The drift classes and what each one implies about where the error was born.
The direction of authority per entity, and the standing exceptions to it.
How past adjudications were decided — the queue history is the case law.

human_roles.does: Owns the compared set, the classification rules, and the safe-class list; watches the drift trend for upstream change.
human_roles.cadence: Weekly trend review; hands-on when a class graduates to auto-fix or a new class appears.
transition_walkthrough_must_cover: Why each auto-fixed class was declared safe, and the evidence behind it.
The fingerprint mechanism and when a full sweep is required.
How to read a drift-trend step change as an upstream process announcement.

failure_design.failure: A fetch failure reads as mass drift — everything unreachable looks missing.
failure_design.response: Distinguish 'absent' from 'unreachable' at the fetch layer. An outage must abort the comparison, not file thousands of missing-copy findings.

failure_design.failure: The adjudication queue backs up and drift findings go stale.
failure_design.response: Depth and age alarms per the human-review-queue pattern; stale findings get re-verified before action, since either side may have changed since detection.

failure_design.failure: People edit the copy because it is easier than editing the source of truth, and auto-fix keeps reverting them.
failure_design.response: Report edits-against-authority per user as a trend. It is a training signal for the client's process owner, not a policing tool — and sometimes it is evidence the declared authority direction is wrong.

manifest_bindings.systems: Every system holding a copy, each with access, rate limits (reconciliation is read-heavy), and gotchas about lag and soft-deletion.
manifest_bindings.entities: The reconciled entity with source_of_truth and also_lives_in filled honestly — this pattern is those two fields turned into a machine.

decisions_expected.tension: Coverage versus alarm noise — what was deliberately excluded and why.
Removing toil versus propagating a misclassification at machine speed, in the direction of authority.
The declared source of truth versus where edits actually happen day to day.

constraints_expected: Any prohibition on writing to either system, and which side of it this flow sits.

metrics.note: Flat and low is health. A rising trend is an upstream process change announcing itself — the single most valuable signal this pattern produces.

metrics.metric: Time from drift occurring to drift detected

maturity.evidence: Designed from the reconciliation halves of intake and batch-action work, not yet shipped standalone. The shape is conservative on purpose — report-only default, no bidirectional writes. Expect the drift-classification taxonomy to be wrong in an instructive way on first contact with a real client.
